intentions"


# Setup 

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE) 

library(readxl)    
library(lubridate)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(ggfixest)
library(HonestDiD)

# power function

power.twoside <- function(betaA,alpha,stderrorE){
  return(pnorm(-abs(betaA)/(stderrorE)-qnorm(1-alpha/2))+pnorm(abs(betaA)/(stderrorE)-qnorm(1-alpha/2)))
}

```

# Data import and cleaning

## Import of the df

The dataframe are available in xls format, with one department per
sheet, so the import is a bit tedious

```{r database import, include=FALSE}
read_excel_allsheets <- function(filename, tibble = FALSE) {
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(filename)
  x <- lapply(sheets, function(X) readxl::read_excel(filename, sheet = X))
  if(!tibble) x <- lapply(x, as.data.frame)
  names(x) <- sheets
  x
}

gn_4001 <- read_excel_allsheets("../data/tableaux-4001-gn.xlsx")
pn_4001 <- read_excel_allsheets("../data/tableaux-4001-pn.xlsx")

```

```{r}

gn_4001 <- gn_4001[-c(1,2, 99:109)]
gn_4001 <-  bind_rows(gn_4001, .id = "department")

pn_4001 <- pn_4001[-c(1,2, 99:109)]
pn_4001 <-  bind_rows(pn_4001, .id = "department")

# First, save the index/libelle index correspondancy 

index_4001 <- gn_4001[1:107, c("Index", "libellé index")]

# Then drop libelle index

gn_4001 <- gn_4001[, -3]
pn_4001 <- pn_4001[, -3]

# Full wide dataset 

gn_4001 <- pivot_longer(gn_4001, cols = !c(department, Index), names_to = "date", values_to = "count")
pn_4001 <- pivot_longer(pn_4001, cols = !c(department, Index), names_to = "date", values_to = "count")

# Add the i mark for conveniency + jurisdiction indicator

gn_4001$jurisdiction <- "gn"
pn_4001$jurisdiction <- "pn"

gn_4001$index <- paste0("i", gn_4001$Index)
pn_4001$index <- paste0("i", pn_4001$Index)

# Extract year and month from date 

gn_4001$year <- substr(gn_4001$date,2,5)
gn_4001$month <- substr(gn_4001$date,7,8)

pn_4001$year <- substr(pn_4001$date,2,5)
pn_4001$month <- substr(pn_4001$date,7,8)

# Select only interesting columns

gn_4001 <- subset(gn_4001, select = c("department", "jurisdiction", "index", "year", "month", "count"))
pn_4001 <- subset(pn_4001, select = c("department", "jurisdiction", "index", "year", "month", "count"))

# We can finally pivot to wide with the offense

gn_4001 <- pivot_wider(gn_4001, names_from = "index", values_from = "count")
pn_4001 <- pivot_wider(pn_4001, names_from = "index", values_from = "count")

# Final merge

gn_pn_4001 <- rbind(gn_4001, pn_4001)

# Clean unused elements

rm(gn_4001, pn_4001, gn_4001_t, pn_4001_t)

```

## Data cleaning and indicators creation

```{r indicators, include=FALSE}

# Treated and neighboring department vector 

dep_w <- c("04", "31","34","38","44","59","60","63","67", "77", "83" ) 

ne_dep <- c("01", "02", "03", "05", "06", "09", "10", "11", "12", "13", "15", "19", "23", "26","27", "30", "32", "35", "42", "45", "49", "51", "56", "57", "62", "65", "68", "69", "73", "76", "80", "81", "82", "84","85", "88", "89", "95")

# did indicators, fixed effects and cluster levels

gn_pn_4001$date <- as.Date(paste0(gn_pn_4001$year, "-", gn_pn_4001$month, "-", "01"), format = "%Y-%m-%d")
gn_pn_4001$post <- ifelse(gn_pn_4001$date >= as.Date("2017-10-01"), 1,0)

gn_pn_4001$post_1_3 <- factor(ifelse(gn_pn_4001$date >= as.Date("2017-10-01") & gn_pn_4001$date < as.Date("2018-03-01"), 1,
                              ifelse(gn_pn_4001$date >= as.Date("2018-03-01") & gn_pn_4001$date < as.Date("2018-08-01"), 2, ifelse(gn_pn_4001$date >= as.Date("2018-08-01") & gn_pn_4001$date <= as.Date("2018-12-01"), 3,0))))



gn_pn_4001$treat <- ifelse(gn_pn_4001$department %in% dep_w & gn_pn_4001$jurisdiction == "gn", 1 ,0)

gn_pn_4001$dep_w <- ifelse(gn_pn_4001$department %in% dep_w, 1, 0) 
gn_pn_4001$dep_n <- ifelse(gn_pn_4001$department %in% ne_dep, 1, 0)

gn_pn_4001$department_month <- paste0(gn_pn_4001$department, "_", gn_pn_4001$month)

gn_pn_4001$jurisdiction_department <- paste0(gn_pn_4001$jurisdiction, "_", gn_pn_4001$department)

# We have population data only since 2006, so we can restrict the dataset

gn_pn_4001 <- subset(gn_pn_4001, subset = year >= 2006)

```

## Import and merge the population per jurisdiction and department 

Source: https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/3698339#consulter

```{r}

# Import and clean

population <- read.csv("../data/population_2006_2021.csv", sep = ',')
population <- population[, c(1:3, 5:20)]

population <- subset(population, subset = !(DEP %in% c("971", "972", "973","974")))


population$DEP <- ifelse(nchar(population$DEP) == 1, str_pad(population$DEP, 2, pad = "0"), as.character(population$DEP))

population$CODGEO <- ifelse(nchar(population$CODGEO) == 4, str_pad(population$CODGEO, 5, pad = "0"), as.character(population$CODGEO)) 

# Pivot population in long format

population <- pivot_longer(population, cols = !c(CODGEO, REG, DEP), names_to = "year", values_to = "population")
population$year <- substr(population$year, 5,8)

```

```{r}

comp_territorial <- read.csv("../data/export-competence-territoriale-pn-gn.csv", sep = ";")

population <- merge(population, subset(comp_territorial, select = c("code_commune", "institution")), by.x = "CODGEO", by.y = "code_commune", all.x = T)

colnames(population) <- c("codgeo", "region", "department", "year", "population", "jurisdiction")

population <- subset(population, subset = complete.cases(jurisdiction))
population$jurisdiction <- tolower(population$jurisdiction)
population$population <- as.numeric(population$population)
# sum by department and jurisdiction 

population_dep_juris <- population %>% group_by(department, jurisdiction, year) %>% summarise(population = sum(population))


# final merge

gn_pn_4001 <- merge(gn_pn_4001, population_dep_juris, by = c("department", "jurisdiction", "year"), all.x = T)

# We can drop all the observations without population = pn for 75, 92, 93, 94

gn_pn_4001 <- subset(gn_pn_4001, subset = complete.cases(population))

```

## Crime level and rate 

```{r data_cleaning, include=FALSE}

# We check the effect of PAVED on 4 indicators : 
# House robery (27 and 28), car stealing (34 and 35), and stealing of motorcycle (36 )

gn_pn_4001$burglary <- gn_pn_4001$i27 + gn_pn_4001$i28
gn_pn_4001$burglary_r <- (gn_pn_4001$burglary/gn_pn_4001$population)*10000

gn_pn_4001$vehicle_theft <-  gn_pn_4001$i34 + gn_pn_4001$i35 + gn_pn_4001$i36
gn_pn_4001$vehicle_theft_r <- (gn_pn_4001$vehicle_theft/gn_pn_4001$population)*10000

# Alternative type of crime: theft and theft from auto 

gn_pn_4001$theft <- gn_pn_4001$i32 + gn_pn_4001$i33
gn_pn_4001$theft_r <- (gn_pn_4001$theft/gn_pn_4001$population)*10000

gn_pn_4001$tfa <- gn_pn_4001$i37 + gn_pn_4001$i38
gn_pn_4001$tfa_r <- (gn_pn_4001$tfa/gn_pn_4001$population)*10000

gn_pn_4001$dealing <- gn_pn_4001$i55
gn_pn_4001$dealing_r <- (gn_pn_4001$dealing/gn_pn_4001$population)*10000

# Create our working base  : exclude paris

gn_pn_4001_province <- subset(gn_pn_4001, subset = !(gn_pn_4001$department %in% c("75", "92", "93", "94")))

```

# Analysis 

We organize the analysis into three parts. For each parts is provided super plots as well as the regression results. The parts are organized as follow: 

1. We compare only Gendarmerie areas. The adopted conterfactual is the Gendarmerie areas which didn't received PAVED. We create a dataset with only Gendarmerie areas.
2. We compare Gendarmerie areas with Police areas. The conterfactual here is the police areas in department which are treated. The intuition is that within a given department, police and gendarmerie areas should behave the same, except when the gendarmerie is now equipped with PAVED. Here, we keep only the treated department, with police and gendarmerie areas
3. We compare the variation between gendarmerie and police areas within control department pre-post paved with the variation between gendarmerie and police areas within treated department pre-post paved. It is a triple difference in difference. Here, we keep all the observations

For each setup, we implement four range of fixed effects: 
1. canonical did (no fe)
2. department + date (two-way fixed effects) 
3. department_month (seasonality)
4. department + date + department_month (full range)

We estimate these models on the rate of burglary and vehicle theft.

Following traditional literature on the subject, we cluster at the level of intervention, which is the jurisdiction x department indicator.

## Dataset creation 

```{r}

# for regressions

df_gendarmerie <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset =  gn_pn_4001_province$jurisdiction == "gn" & gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2015 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)

df_gendarmerie_police <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset = gn_pn_4001_province$dep_w == 1 & gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2015 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)

df_didid <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset = gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2015 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)

# all months of the regression window, used as x-axis limits in event-study plots

all_dates <- sort(unique(df_didid$date))

# for plots

df_gendarmerie_plot <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset = gn_pn_4001_province$jurisdiction == "gn" & gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2010 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)

df_gendarmerie_police_plot <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset = gn_pn_4001_province$dep_w == 1 & gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2010 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)

df_didid_plot <- subset(gn_pn_4001_province, subset = gn_pn_4001_province$year >= 2010 & gn_pn_4001_province$year < 2019)


# Indicator for plot 

df_gendarmerie <- df_gendarmerie %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(
    date < as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Pre",
    date >= as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Post"
  ),
  group = paste0(period, "_", treat) # Creates four groups: Pre_0, Pre_1, Post_0, Post_1
  )

df_gendarmerie_police <- df_gendarmerie_police %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(
    date < as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Pre",
    date >= as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Post"
  ),
  group = paste0(period, "_", jurisdiction) # Creates four groups: Pre_0, Pre_1, Post_0, Post_1
  )

df_didid <- df_didid %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(
    date < as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Pre",
    date >= as.Date("2017-10-01") ~ "Post"
  ),
  group = paste0(period, "_", jurisdiction) # Creates four groups: Pre_0, Pre_1, Post_0, Post_1
  )

```

# Analysis: catchment area outside of the control group

## Estimation: comparing gendarmerie areas

### Plot

```{r}

ggplot(df_gendarmerie, aes(y = burglary_r, x = date, color = as.factor(dep_w), group = as.factor(dep_w))) + 
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "line") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.Date("2017-10-01"))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 month", date_labels =  "%b %Y", limits = as.Date(c('2015-01-01','2018-12-01'))) + 
  geom_smooth(aes(group = group), method = "lm", se = TRUE) + 
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1), legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 16)) + 
  labs(colour = "Group", y = "Burglary rate (per 10000)", x = NULL) + 
  scale_color_manual(values=c('red3','forestgreen'), labels=c("Control", "Treatment")) +
  scale_y_continuous()

ggsave("../output/counterfactual_gendarmerie_burglary_r.pdf", width = 2700, height = 1800, units = "px")

# vehicle theft

ggplot(df_gendarmerie, aes(y = vehicle_theft_r, x = date, color = as.factor(dep_w), group = as.factor(dep_w))) + 
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "line") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.Date("2017-10-01"))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 month", date_labels =  "%b %Y", limits = as.Date(c('2015-01-01','2018-12-01'))) + 
  geom_smooth(aes(group = group), method = "lm", se = TRUE) + 
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1), legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 16)) + 
  labs(colour = "Group", y = "Vehicle theft rate (per 10000)", x = NULL) + 
  scale_color_manual(values=c('red3','forestgreen'), labels=c("Control", "Treatment")) +
  scale_y_continuous()

ggsave("../output/counterfactual_gendarmerie_vehicle_theft_r.pdf", width = 2700, height = 1800, units = "px")

```



### Regression 

Models from this section are refered as "cg_" ( counterfactual gendarmerie)

First, create a fixed effect as interaction of treatment and period, for trend correction 

```{r}

df_gendarmerie$trend_correction_treat <- ifelse(df_gendarmerie$dep_w == 1, df_gendarmerie$period, 0)


df_gendarmerie$trend_correction_control <- ifelse(df_gendarmerie$dep_w == 0, df_gendarmerie$period, 0)

```


#### Burglary

```{r}


cg_burglary1 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + treat + dep_n + post:treat + dep_n:post, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
cg_burglary2 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + treat + dep_n + post:treat + dep_n:post | jurisdiction_department + date, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
cg_burglary3 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + treat + dep_n + post:treat + dep_n:post | department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
cg_burglary4 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + treat + dep_n + post:treat + dep_n:post | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

etable(cg_burglary1, cg_burglary2, cg_burglary3, cg_burglary4)

file_path <- "../output/tables/conterfact_gendarmerie_catchment_burglary.tex"
sink(file_path)
etable(cg_burglary1, cg_burglary2, cg_burglary3, cg_burglary4, tex = T)
sink()

# Power 

se_tau_cg_burglary4 <- se(cg_burglary4)["post:treat"]
coeff_tau_cg_burglary4 <- coef(cg_burglary4)["post:treat"]

paste0("The power of our test of the treatment parameters is ", power.twoside(coeff_tau_cg_burglary4, 0.05, se_tau_cg_burglary4), " which means we have a ", power.twoside(coeff_tau_cg_burglary4, 0.05, se_tau_cg_burglary4), " probability of detecting such effect if it was the true effect")

```

Event study plot

```{r}

cg_burglary1_es <- feols(
  burglary_r ~  i(date, treat, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | date + jurisdiction_department,
  data = subset(df_gendarmerie, dep_n == 0),

)

summary(cg_burglary1_es)

  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), line = element_line(linewidth = 0.4)) +

    title = "Event study: Burglary rate - counterfactual Gendarmerie (TWFE)",
    x = "Date",
```

## Estimation: comparing gendarmerie with police areas

Here the notation are a little bit more tricky: the treatment indicators is the jurisdiction, as we are working within treated department, but only the gendarmerie received PAVED in these departments.

### Regression

The model from this section are refered as "gp_" (gendarmerie and police comparison). First we start by relevel jurisdiction for pn to be the reference: 

```{r}

df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction <- as.factor(df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction)
df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction <- relevel(df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction, "pn")

```

#### Burglary

```{r}

gp_burglary1 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + jurisdiction + post:jurisdiction, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
gp_burglary2 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + jurisdiction + post:jurisdiction | jurisdiction_department + date, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
gp_burglary3 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + jurisdiction + post:jurisdiction | department_month, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')
gp_burglary4 <- feols(burglary_r ~ post + jurisdiction + post:jurisdiction | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

etable(gp_burglary1, gp_burglary2, gp_burglary3, gp_burglary4)

file_path <- "../output/tables/conterfact_police_no_catchment_burglary.tex"
sink(file_path)
etable(gp_burglary1, gp_burglary2, gp_burglary3, gp_burglary4, tex = T)
sink()


```

Event study 

```{r}


df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction_gn <- ifelse(df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction == "gn", 1, 0)
```

# Robustness check: Count regression 

In this section, we expand on the results obtained for the Gendarmerie areas only analysis. We spotted a negative effect of 0.2 percentage points. However, we used an OLS regression to obtain these results, based on an outcome which is essentially a count. 

```{r}

hist(df_gendarmerie$burglary_r)
hist(df_gendarmerie$vehicle_theft_r)

```
If we look at the histogram of the rate of burglary and vehicle theft, we can observe that the distributions are not standard distribution. Then, we estimate a count  regressions to ensure that our results are not due to a wrong model choice. 

GLM with count distribution use a log link function. Thus, we have to check the pre-trend with the log of the crime level. 

### Plot

```{r}

ggplot(df_gendarmerie, aes(y = log(burglary), x = date, color = factor(treat), group = factor(treat))) + 
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "line") 

ggplot(df_gendarmerie, aes(y = log(vehicle_theft), x = date, color = factor(treat), group = factor(treat))) + 
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "line") 

```

Still quite convincing, we can proceed to the regressions.

### Regression

Since we are interested in the rate of crime, we add the population as an offset in the specification. 

But the question is: which kind of regression to use? Poisson regression needs the mean of the distribution to be roughly equal to the variance, which is clearly not the case as we have a strong overdispersion. Negative Binomial can be an alternative, but require the distribution to be exactly negative binomial, which is not the case. Quasi poisson regression can be an answer. 

Both negative binomial and quasi poisson are made to model over-dispersed outcomes. However, the quasi poisson assumes that the variance of the model is linear to the mean, while the negative binomial assumes it is quadratic. 

```{r}

g_poisson_burglary1 <- fenegbin(burglary ~ post + treat + post:treat, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', offset = ~log(population))
g_poisson_burglary2 <- fenegbin(burglary ~ post:treat | department + date, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', offset = ~log(population))
g_poisson_burglary3 <- fenegbin(burglary ~ post + post:treat | department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', offset = ~log(population))
g_poisson_burglary4 <- fenegbin(burglary ~ post:treat | department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', offset = ~log(population))

etable(g_poisson_burglary1, g_poisson_burglary2, g_poisson_burglary3, g_poisson_burglary4)

```

```{r}

g_poisson_vehicle_theft1 <- feglm(vehicle_theft ~ post + treat + post:treat, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', family=quasipoisson, offset = log(df_gendarmerie$population))
g_poisson_vehicle_theft2 <- feglm(vehicle_theft ~ post:treat | department + date, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', family=quasipoisson, offset =log(df_gendarmerie$population))
g_poisson_vehicle_theft3 <- feglm(vehicle_theft ~ post:treat | department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', family=quasipoisson, offset = log(df_gendarmerie$population))

g_poisson_vehicle_theft4 <- fenegbin(vehicle_theft ~ post:treat | department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department', offset = log(df_gendarmerie$population))

# results

etable(g_poisson_vehicle_theft1, g_poisson_vehicle_theft2, g_poisson_vehicle_theft3, g_poisson_vehicle_theft4)

```

```{r}
library(fixest)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(broom)
library(xtable)

# Named mapping of models to the term to extract
coef_map <- c(
  cg_burglary4_percentage      = "post:treat",
  cg_vehicle_theft4_percentage = "post:treat ",
  gp_burglary4_percentage      = "post:jurisdictiongn",
  gp_vehicle_theft4_percentage = "post:jurisdictiongn",
  cd3_burglary4_percentage     = "post:dep_w:jurisdictiongn",
  cd3_vehicle_theft4_percentage= "post:dep_w:jurisdictiongn"
)

models <- list(
  cg_burglary4_percentage      = cg_burglary4_percentage,
  cg_vehicle_theft4_percentage = cg_vehicle_theft4_percentage,
  gp_burglary4_percentage      = gp_burglary4_percentage,
  gp_vehicle_theft4_percentage = gp_vehicle_theft4_percentage,
  cd3_burglary4_percentage     = cd3_burglary4_percentage,
  cd3_vehicle_theft4_percentage= cd3_vehicle_theft4_percentage
)
# Function to extract stats from a fixest poisson model
extract_info <- function(model_name, model_obj) {
  
  est <- broom::tidy(model_obj, conf.int = TRUE)
  
  est %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name,
      
      # IRR and CI
      IRR = exp(estimate),
      IRR_low = exp(conf.low),
      IRR_high = exp(conf.high),
      
      # Percent effects
      pct =  (IRR - 1) * 100,
      pct_low = (IRR_low - 1) * 100,
      pct_high = (IRR_high - 1) * 100
    ) %>%
    select(
      model, term, estimate, IRR,  std.error,
      pct, pct_low, pct_high
    )
}

# Build full table
results_table <- as.data.frame(map2_df(names(models), models, extract_info))
results_table <- cbind(subset(results_table, select = c(model, term)),  apply(subset(results_table, select = -c(model, term)), 2, as.numeric))
results_table <- cbind(subset(results_table, select = c(model, term)),  apply(subset(results_table, select = -c(model, term)), 2, function(x) round(x, 2)))

results_table

xtable(results_table)

```

```{r}
  cd3_burglary4     = cd3_burglary4,
  cd3_vehicle_theft2= cd3_vehicle_theft2,
  cd3_vehicle_theft4= cd3_vehicle_theft4
)
# Function to extract stats from a fixest poisson model
extract_info <- function(model_name, model_obj) {

  alpha_95 <- 0.05
  alpha_90 <- 0.10

  z_95 <- qnorm(1 - alpha_95 / 2)
  z_90 <- qnorm(1 - alpha_90 / 2)

  term_of_interest <- coef_map_pp[[model_name]]

  broom::tidy(model_obj) %>%
    filter(term == term_of_interest) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name,

      # --- Confidence intervals ---
      ci95_low = estimate - z_95 * std.error,
      ci95_high = estimate + z_95 * std.error,

      ci90_low = estimate - z_90 * std.error,
      ci90_high = estimate + z_90 * std.error
    ) %>%
    select(
      model, term, estimate, std.error,
      ci90_low, ci90_high,
      ci95_low, ci95_high
    )
}

# Build full table
results_table_pp <- map2_df(
  names(models_pp),
  models_pp,
  extract_info
)

results_table_pp

model_order <- c(
  "cg_burglary2",
  "cg_burglary4",
  "cg_vehicle_theft2",
  "cg_vehicle_theft4",
  "gp_burglary2",
  "gp_burglary4",
  "gp_vehicle_theft2",
  "gp_vehicle_theft4",
  "cd3_burglary2",
  "cd3_burglary4",
  "cd3_vehicle_theft2",
  "cd3_vehicle_theft4"
  )


# right names for models

model_labels <- c(
  cg_burglary2        = "Gendarmerie counterfactual – Burglary (TWFE)",
  cg_burglary4        = "Gendarmerie counterfactual – Burglary (ATWFE)",
  cg_vehicle_theft2  = "Gendarmerie counterfactual – Vehicle theft (TWFE)",
  cg_vehicle_theft4  = "Gendarmerie counterfactual – Vehicle theft (ATWFE)",
  gp_burglary2       = "Police counterfactual – Burglary (TWFE)",

  gp_vehicle_theft2  = "Police counterfactual – Vehicle theft (TWFE)",
  gp_vehicle_theft4  = "Police counterfactual – Vehicle theft (ATWFE)",
  cd3_burglary2      = "DiDiD – Burglary (TWFE)",

  cd3_vehicle_theft2 = "DiDiD – Vehicle theft (TWFE)",
  cd3_vehicle_theft4 = "DiDiD – Vehicle theft (ATWFE)"
)

results_table_pp <- results_table_pp %>%
  mutate(
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = model_order,

    )
  )


# plot

ggplot(results_table_pp,
       aes(y = as.factor(model), x = estimate)) +

  # --- 95% CI (thin) ---
  geom_errorbarh(
```

## Placebo and randomization 

```{r}


# Candidate placebo dates (monthly)
placebo_dates <- seq(
  as.Date("2015-02-01"),
  as.Date("2018-11-01"),
  by = "month"
)

true_treat_date <- as.Date("2017-10-01")

# gendarmerie 

run_placebo_did_burglary <- function(df, placebo_date) {
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(post_placebo = as.integer(date >= placebo_date))
  
  m_burglary <- feols(
    burglary_r ~ post_placebo + treat + dep_n + post_placebo:treat + dep_n:post_placebo |
      jurisdiction_department + date + department_month,
    data = df,
    cluster = "jurisdiction_department"
  )
  
  coef(m_burglary)["post_placebo:treat"]
}

run_placebo_did_vehicle_theft <- function(df, placebo_date) {
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(post_placebo = as.integer(date >= placebo_date))
  
  m_vehicle_theft <- feols(
    vehicle_theft_r ~ post_placebo + treat + dep_n + post_placebo:treat + dep_n:post_placebo |
      jurisdiction_department + date + department_month,
    data = df,
    cluster = "jurisdiction_department"
  )
  
  coef(m_vehicle_theft)["post_placebo:treat"]
}

# police

run_placebo_did_police_burglary <- function(df, placebo_date) {
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(post_placebo = as.integer(date >= placebo_date))
  
  m_burglary <- feols(
    burglary_r ~ post_placebo + jurisdiction + post_placebo:jurisdiction |
      jurisdiction_department + date + department_month,
    data = df,
    cluster = "jurisdiction_department"
  )
  
  coef(m_burglary)["post_placebo:jurisdictiongn"]
}

  df <- df %>%

}

    data = df,

  )
  
  coef(m_burglary)["post_placebo:dep_w:jurisdictiongn"]
}


run_placebo_didid_vehicle_theft <- function(df, placebo_date) {
```

## Short and long term effect

The treatment period is divided in 3 

```{r}

df_didid$jurisdiction <- as.factor(df_didid$jurisdiction)
df_didid$jurisdiction <- relevel(df_didid$jurisdiction, "pn")

df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction <- as.factor(df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction)

df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction <- relevel(df_gendarmerie_police$jurisdiction, "pn")

cg_burglary4_slterm <- feols(burglary_r ~ post_1_3 + treat + dep_n + post_1_3:treat + post_1_3:post | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

cg_vehicle_theft4_slterm <- feols(vehicle_theft_r ~ post_1_3 + treat + dep_n + post_1_3:treat + dep_n:post_1_3 | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

gp_vehicle_theft4_slterm <- feols(vehicle_theft_r ~ post_1_3 + jurisdiction + post_1_3:jurisdiction | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

cd3_burglary4_slterm <- feols(burglary_r ~ post_1_3*dep_w*jurisdiction + post_1_3*dep_n | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_didid, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

cd3_vehicle_theft4_slterm <- feols(vehicle_theft_r ~ post_1_3*dep_w*jurisdiction + post_1_3*dep_n | jurisdiction_department + date + department_month, df_didid, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

etable(cg_burglary4_slterm, cg_vehicle_theft4_slterm, gp_burglary4_slterm, gp_vehicle_theft4_slterm, cd3_burglary4_slterm, cd3_vehicle_theft4_slterm)

sink()
```

## Honest DiD approach 

Run in parallel 

```{r}
library(doParallel)
registerDoParallel(cores = 10)

```


Burglary

```{r}

# Baseline model, event study 

cg_burglary1_es <- feols(
  burglary_r ~  i(date, treat, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | date + jurisdiction_department,
  data = subset(df_gendarmerie, dep_n == 0),
  cluster = ~ jurisdiction_department
)

gp_burglary1_es <- feols(burglary_r ~ i(date, jurisdiction_gn, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | jurisdiction_department + date, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

d3_burglary1_es <- feols(burglary_r ~ i(date, dep_w*jurisdiction_gn, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | jurisdiction_department + date, df_didid, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')


# Save coefficients
betahat_cg_burglary1_es <- summary(cg_burglary1_es)$coefficients
betahat_gp_burglary1_es <- summary(gp_burglary1_es)$coefficients
betahat_d3_burglary1_es <- summary(d3_burglary1_es)$coefficients

# Save the covariance matrix
sigma_cg_burglary1_es <- summary(cg_burglary1_es)$cov.scaled
sigma_gp_burglary1_es <- summary(gp_burglary1_es)$cov.scaled
sigma_d3_burglary1_es <- summary(d3_burglary1_es)$cov.scaled

#

delta_rm_results_cg_burglary1_es <- createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(
    betahat = betahat_cg_burglary1_es, #coefficients
    sigma = sigma_cg_burglary1_es, #covariance matrix
    numPrePeriods = 32, #num. of pre-treatment coefs
    numPostPeriods = 15, #num. of post-treatment coefs
    Mbarvec = seq(0.5,2,by=0.5), #values of Mbar
    parallel = TRUE
  )

delta_rm_results_gp_burglary1_es <- createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(
    betahat = betahat_gp_burglary1_es, #coefficients
    sigma = sigma_gp_burglary1_es, #covariance matrix
    numPrePeriods = 32, #num. of pre-treatment coefs
    numPostPeriods = 15, #num. of post-treatment coefs
    Mbarvec = seq(0.5,2,by=0.5), #values of Mbar
    parallel = TRUE 
  )


delta_rm_results_d3_burglary1_es <- createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(
    betahat = betahat_d3_burglary1_es, #coefficients
    sigma = sigma_d3_burglary1_es, #covariance matrix
    numPrePeriods = 32, #num. of pre-treatment coefs
    numPostPeriods = 15, #num. of post-treatment coefs
    Mbarvec = seq(0.5,2,by=0.5), #values of Mbar
    parallel = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}

library(HonestDiD)

# Baseline model, event study 

cg_vehicle_theft1_es <- feols(
  vehicle_theft_r ~  i(date, treat, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | date + jurisdiction_department,
  data = subset(df_gendarmerie, dep_n == 0),
  cluster = ~ jurisdiction_department
)

gp_vehicle_theft1_es <- feols(vehicle_theft_r ~ i(date, jurisdiction_gn, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | jurisdiction_department + date, df_gendarmerie_police, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')

d3_vehicle_theft1_es <- feols(vehicle_theft_r ~ i(date, dep_w*jurisdiction_gn, ref = as.Date("2017-09-01")) | jurisdiction_department + date, df_didid, cluster = 'jurisdiction_department')


# Save coefficients
betahat_cg_vehicle_theft1_es <- summary(cg_vehicle_theft1_es)$coefficients
betahat_gp_vehicle_theft1_es <- summary(gp_vehicle_theft1_es)$coefficients
betahat_d3_vehicle_theft1_es <- summary(d3_vehicle_theft1_es)$coefficients

# Save the covariance matrix

sigma_gp_vehicle_theft1_es <- summary(gp_vehicle_theft1_es)$cov.scaled
sigma_d3_vehicle_theft1_es <- summary(d3_vehicle_theft1_es)$cov.scaled

    betahat = betahat_cg_vehicle_theft1_es, #coefficients

    numPostPeriods = 15, #num. of post-treatment coefs
```
